title: Coordinate singularity or cone point?
promptMarkdown:
Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$. On the punctured plane $M=\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}$ let $g_\alpha$ be the Riemannian metric that reads
$$g_\alpha=dr^2+\alpha^2r^2\,d\theta^2$$
in the polar chart $P^{-1}$ of exercise 2 on the slit plane, and in the same form in every polar chart whose slit lies along another ray. (The coefficients do not depend on $\theta$, and two such charts differ on each component of their overlap by a constant shift of $\theta$, so these expressions agree and define one smooth metric on $M$; take this as given.) For $\alpha=1$ this is the Euclidean metric of exercise 2. State your conventions before you begin.

1. Compute $\det(g_{ij})$ in the polar chart for $g_\alpha$ and for $g_1$, and compare their behaviour as $r\to0$.
2. Show that $\Psi(r,\theta)=(r\cos\alpha\theta,\;r\sin\alpha\theta)$ on $(0,\infty)\times(0,2\pi)$ gives an injective isometric map from the slit plane with $g_\alpha$ into $E^2$, and describe its image. Deduce that every point of $M$ has a neighbourhood isometric to an open subset of $E^2$.
3. Write $g_\alpha$ in the Cartesian chart $(x,y)$ of $M$. Show that its coefficients are bounded on $M$ and that, since $\alpha\neq1$, at least one of them has no limit as $(x,y)\to(0,0)$.
4. Show that $g_\alpha(v,v)\ge\big(dr(v)\big)^2$ for every tangent vector $v$ of $M$. Deduce that every piecewise $C^1$ curve in $M$ from a point with $r=r_1$ to a point with $r=r_2$ has $g_\alpha$-length at least $|r_2-r_1|$, and, for two points on a common ray, exhibit a curve of exactly that length. Compute the $g_\alpha$-length of the circle $r=\varepsilon$.
5. Suppose there were a chart $(U,\varphi)$ of the plane with $0\in U$, such that $\varphi$ restricted to $U\setminus\{0\}$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image for the usual smooth structure, and such that the coefficients of $g_\alpha$ in this chart extend smoothly to all of $\varphi(U)$ and are positive definite at $\varphi(0)$. Let $h$ be the resulting Riemannian metric on $U$. You may use without proof the following fact, which needs the exponential map (unit 3) and is not proved in units 1 and 2:

   **(F)** If $(N,h)$ is a Riemannian surface and $p\in N$, then for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ the points at $h$-distance exactly $\varepsilon$ from $p$ form a closed curve whose length $L(\varepsilon)$ satisfies $L(\varepsilon)/\varepsilon\to2\pi$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.

   Show that for small $\varepsilon$ the points of $U$ at $h$-distance exactly $\varepsilon$ from $0$ are the points with $r=\varepsilon$, and use (F) to reach a contradiction.
6. In one paragraph headed 'coordinates' and one headed 'geometry', explain why the degeneration of $g_1$ at $r=0$ belongs to the polar chart while that of $g_\alpha$ belongs to the space, and say which of your computations in parts 1 to 5 tell the two cases apart and which do not.
hintLadder: In the polar chart the coefficient matrix is diagonal. For part 2, compute $\partial_r\Psi$ and $\partial_\theta\Psi$ and their Euclidean inner products, as for a Gram matrix.
For part 3, express $dr$ and $r\,d\theta$ in terms of $dx$ and $dy$, then compare the coefficient of $dx^2$ along the two coordinate axes.
For part 4, write $v=v^r\partial_r+v^\theta\partial_\theta$, and compare the length integrand of a curve with $|d(r\circ\gamma)/dt|$.
For the lower bound on $h$-distance in part 5, take the last time at which a curve from $0$ to $q$ is at $0$, and apply part 4 to the rest of the curve.
For the upper bound, travel radially from a point very near $0$ out to $q$, and use that the distance of $h$ induces the topology of $U$ (Proposition 5.10).

criteria.criterion: det(g_ij) = α²r² for g_α and r² for g_1, both tending to 0 like r²; recognised that the determinant only reports that the polar chart degenerates at r = 0, and does so identically for both metrics.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both determinants and the limited reading.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Determinants right, reading missing or overstated.

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Wrong, or the vanishing read as proof of a coordinate singularity.

criteria.criterion: ∂_rΨ and ∂_θΨ computed with Gram matrix diag(1, α²r²); Ψ shown injective with image the open sector of angle 2πα; every point of M placed in a slit plane where the same computation applies.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Pull-back, injectivity, image and the covering of M.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Pull-back right, injectivity or image or covering missing.

criteria.criterion: g_xx = (x² + α²y²)/(x² + y²), g_xy = (1 − α²)xy/(x² + y²), g_yy = (α²x² + y²)/(x² + y²); bounded; g_xx tends to 1 along the x-axis and to α² along the y-axis, so it has no limit; recognised as the failure of one chart only.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Coefficients, bounds, missing limit and the limited reading.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Coefficients right, but the result read as excluding every chart.

criteria.criterion: g_α(v,v) = (v^r)² + α²r²(v^θ)² ≥ (dr(v))², with r a global function on M; length at least |r₂ − r₁| by integrating |d(r∘γ)/dt|; radial segments attain it; the circle r = ε has length 2παε.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Inequality, bound, attaining curves and the circle.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Circle length right, bound argued only inside one polar chart or attaining curves missing.

criteria.criterion: d_h(0,q) = r(q) for q near 0, the lower bound from the last visit to 0 and part 4, the upper bound from radial segments and Proposition 5.10; the h-distance circle of radius ε identified as r = ε, of length 2παε, contradicting (F) since α ≠ 1.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both inequalities justified and the contradiction drawn.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Contradiction drawn with one inequality asserted, or the distance circle identified without argument.

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Missing, or a chart excluded by part 3 alone.

criteria.criterion: Separate paragraphs: for g_1 a chart (Cartesian) removes the degeneracy; for g_α none can, because circumference over radius of small distance circles is an isometry invariant equal to 2πα, not 2π; parts 1 to 3 identified as unable to decide and parts 4 and 5 as deciding.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both paragraphs, with the invariant named.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Conclusion right, paragraphs merged or the deciding computation not named.

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Claims both degenerations are coordinate effects.

difficulty.basis: Routine computations (a determinant, a Gram matrix, Cartesian coefficients, two lengths) lead to a distance argument with two inequalities, one of which needs Proposition 5.10, and to an appeal to a stated fact about small distance circles.
